name: Guibei Zhuang
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Zhang Junru et al. 1999, Zhuangyu fangyan yanjiu [A study of Zhuang dialects], covering northern Zhuang varieties incl. Guibei; no online copy reachable

sources.citation: Chen, Honglei, Chalermsak Pikulsri & Surapol Nesusin. 2025. Prosodic structure and rhythmic patterns in Zhuang folk songs: a metrical phonological perspective. Forum for Linguistic Studies 7(12): 1698-1713. doi:10.30564/fls.v7i12.11954.
sources.note: Annotates 'prosodic word stress' vs beats in a sung corpus from 12 Guangxi cities (northern/southern/central dialect regions); never states where lexical word stress falls in spoken Zhuang and does not treat Guibei separately. Not a usable stress statement.

sources.citation: Castro, Andy & Bruce Hansen. 2010. Hongshui He Zhuang dialect intelligibility survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-025. 110 pp.
sources.note: No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the report; covers Central/Eastern Hongshuihe and Liuqian varieties, not Guibei (Guibei only in a population table, p. 8 area). Tone analysis only.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2007. The power of language over the past: Tai settlement and Tai linguistics in southern China and northern Vietnam. In Studies in Southeast Asian Linguistics, 39-63. Bangkok.
Huang, P. 2007. Sinification of the Zhuang people, culture, and their language. SEALS XII (2002) papers, 89-100. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Scan with no text layer; sociolinguistic topic; not scanned and not read for stress (Glottolog tags it socling for all ten Northern Zhuang codes incl. zgb).

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University.
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction; 'stress' appears only in the discussion of Proto-Tai sesquisyllables (unstressed minor + stressed major syllable). No statement about word stress in Guibei Zhuang (uses Donglan, Hechi, Huanjiang, Longsheng, Rong'an as data points for segments/tones only).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-027 (split of Northern Zhuang [ccx]; creation of zgb Guibei Zhuang etc.). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative change request. Names Zhang Junru et al. 1999 (壮语方言研究) and Chen & Li 2005 as its sources.

sources.citation: Coyaud, Maurice. 1987. Les langues dans le monde chinois. Paris: Pour l'Analyse du Folklore. pp. 127-128 (§3.4 Phonologie, zhuang) and pp. 49-50 (§2.5 Les écritures zhuang). Rosetta Project excerpts.
sources.note: Silent: lists consonants, vowels and six tones (three in checked syllables) of (standard/Wuming-type) Northern Zhuang; no mention of accent or stress. Not Guibei-specific.

sources.citation: Luo, Yongxian. 2008. Zhuang. In Anthony V. N. Diller, Jerold A. Edmondson & Yongxian Luo (eds), The Tai-Kadai languages, 317-377. London & New York: Routledge.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Most authoritative modern English sketch of (Northern) Zhuang phonology and grammar; would settle whether Zhuang is described as having no word stress or final-syllable prominence; search-inside blocked from our machine.

sources.citation: Wei Qingwen 韦庆稳 & Qin Guosheng 覃国生. 1980. 壮语简志 Zhuàngyǔ jiǎnzhì [A brief description of Zhuang]. Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe.

sources.note: The standard Chinese sketch of Zhuang (Wuming/Northern-based) in the 中国少数民族语言简志丛书 series, whose phonology chapters routinely include a sentence on 重音; would give at least a second-hand Northern Zhuang statement applicable to Guibei with an identity caveat.

sources.citation: Zhang Junru, Liang Min, Ouyang Jueya, Zheng Yiqing, Li Xulian & Xie Jianyou. 1999. 壮语方言研究 Zhuàngyǔ fāngyán yánjiū [A study of Zhuang dialects]. Chengdu: Sichuan Minzu Chubanshe. 938 pp. ISBN 7540922931.

sources.note: The reference dialect survey of Zhuang (36 points incl. Guibei points Hechi, Yishan, Nandan, Donglan, Huanjiang, Longsheng, Rong'an); the ISO split of zgb and the earlier scan both rest on it; its general phonology chapter is the most likely place for a Chinese statement on 重音/轻重音 in Northern Zhuang.

sources.citation: Wei Feng & Jerold A. Edmondson. 1997. The tonal cylinder in Sanfang Zhuang. In Jerold A. Edmondson & David B. Solnit (eds), Comparative Kadai: The Tai branch, 35-55. Dallas: SIL & University of Texas at Arlington (Publications in Linguistics 124).

sources.note: The only English-language phonetic/phonological study of a specifically Guibei variety (Sanfang, Rongshui); a tone study that may remark on stress/prominence; SIL says 'Not Available Online'.
